task: Make canonical host proof distinguish binary availability from noninteractive reviewer execution readiness and observable launcher correctness.
outcome: A user runs lattice review_host_availability_probe --storyId=B-d8ef --json and sees codex/claude/agy rows with executionReady/progressMode/failureKind; fallback diagnostics then use reviewReadyHostCount and name wrong launcher/auth/silent-output causes instead of appearing to hang.
facts: Current review_host_availability_probe records executable path plus --version responsiveness only.
Claude --print is valid but final-output oriented; observable reviewer execution should use claude --print --verbose --output-format=stream-json, optionally with --include-hook-events.
Claude stream-json without --verbose was observed to be the wrong shape for realtime visibility.
Installed agy CLI rejects --prompt-file and supports --print/--prompt plus --print-timeout.
Codex login status can appear logged in while codex exec fails with token_invalidated or refresh_token_invalidated.
Decision: extend the existing host availability probe with bounded launcher-readiness rows rather than adding a separate required command.
Decision: non-human degraded fallback consumes reviewReadyHostCount/executionReadyHostCount, with legacy version-only events not eligible as review-ready proof.
constraints: Do not read or copy auth-profile token files directly.
Do not run omx or touch .omx.
Do not mutate unrelated dirty main files.
Do not promote local host evidence into release readiness or retired completion fields.
Keep probes bounded and avoid expensive long live LLM calls in routine paths.
Process facts consumed by DONE gates must be schema-checked and registered.
